wasteCodes.practice: (1) Transportation, Labelling and Storage of Hazardous waste at the Hazardous waste storage house. The hazardous waste in the container/drum shall be transported to the hazardous waste storage house with the corresponding Hazardous Waste Label and appropriate GHS hazard and transport pictograms. The quantity/volume of waste must be recorded for monitoring. It must be inspected to ensure that the drum/container containing the waste doesn’t have leaks before storing the waste. The hazardous waste in the hazardous waste storage house must be ensure that that liquid or sludge wastes are placed in a secondary containment to prevent spills/leaks and from entering into the drainage or sewerage system. (2) Pull-out/collection of Hazardous Waste by an Accredited Transporter. The hazardous waste must be pull-out by an accredited transporter and TSD facility. Upon hazardous waste pull-out, it must be ensure that the Transporter have the following: Valid Transport Permit, Hazardous Waste Manifest Form, and must refer to the Transport Permit on the quantity or volume permitted/granted by DENR. The manifest form must be properly fill-up and shall be prepared every transport. The accredited hazardous waste transporter shall pull-out/collect the hazardous waste stored at the hazardous waste storage house and transport the waste to the TSD Facility. The accredited TSD Facility shall properly treat, store and dispose the hazardous wastes off-site. We shall coordinate with the TSD Facility and shall obtain CERTIFICATE OF TREATMENT (COT) for the waste treated to be filed for record keeping and reference.

'1.Handling of busted flourescent lamps(BFL)-When busted flourescent lamps are removed and replaced with new lamps,the used lamps shoulde be placed in an empty flourescent box and/or properly packaged/wrapped individually in the cardboard boxes.Make sure to completely seal the box to prevent any leaks from bulb breakage or wrap it with newspaper and place it in a secure container.-Do not tape lamps together.-The boxes/container containing busted flourescent lamps (BFL)must be labeled using the prescribed hazardous waste label and placard.Please refer to attachement 2.Storage of busted FLOURESCENT LAMPS(BFL)-Separate the busted flourescent lamps from other wastes produced by it.To avoid breakage and stored at safe area._x000D_ If a fluorescent lamp breaks, you should: _x000D_ _x000D_ Ventilate the area: Open windows to allow the room to ventilate. _x000D_ _x000D_ Wear protective equipment: Wear eye protection, respiratory protection, and gloves to prevent irritation and lacerations. _x000D_ Sweep up the fragments: Carefully sweep up all the fragments with a wet towel. _x000D_ Place the fragments in a sealed container: Place the fragments in an impermeable container and label it appropriately. _x000D_ Dispose of the fragments: Dispose of the fragments per applicable federal, state, and local regulations. _x000D_ _x000D_ Additional tips Do not vacuum lamp fragments, Clean up all visible lamp pieces before vacuuming, and Follow all disposal instructions._x000D_ _x000D_ Why take these precautions?_x000D_ Broken fluorescent lamps can release mercury vapor and sharp edges from broken fixture components. Although the exposure to mercury is extremely small, you should take precautions to avoid irritation and lacerations._x000D_ Removing the broken lamp debris and ventilating the area for 15 minutes (if possible) is recommended. Do not vacuum lamp fragments. Clean-up all visible lamp pieces before vacuuming._x000D_ If a mercury-containing lamp breaks, immediately leave the area, then return wearing gloves and carefully collect all visible glass fragments and mercury powder using stiff paper or cardboard, avoiding sweeping which can disperse the mercury; use tape to pick up tiny particles, and then wipe the area clean with damp paper towels; place all debris in a sealed container and dispose of properly according to local regulations; ventilate the room by opening windows and doors; wash your hands thoroughly afterwards. _x000D_ Key steps to follow:_x000D_ _x000D_ Leave the area: Immediately exit the room and close the door to prevent further spread of mercury vapor. _x000D_ _x000D_ Wear protective gear: Put on disposable gloves before attempting cleanup. _x000D_ Secure the broken bulb: Carefully pick up large glass fragments with cardboard or stiff paper. _x000D_ Collect mercury powder: Use tape to pick up small mercury particles and dust from the surface. _x000D_ Wipe the area: Dampen a paper towel or wet wipe and gently wipe the affected area. _x000D_ Dispose properly: Place all glass fragments, paper, tape, and used cleaning materials in a sealed plastic bag or container. _x000D_ Ventilate the room: Open windows and doors to air out the area. _x000D_ Wash hands thoroughly: Wash your hands with soap and water after cleanup. _x000D_ _x000D_ Important points to remember:_x000D_ _x000D_ Do not use a vacuum cleaner:_x000D_ Vacuuming can spread mercury vapor further by sucking it into the vacuum cleaner. _x000D_ _x000D_ Do not flush mercury down the drain:_x000D_ This can contaminate your plumbing system. _x000D_ Check local disposal guidelines:_x000D_ Contact your local waste management service to find out the proper disposal method for broken mercury-containing lamps. _x000D_ Consider professional cleanup for large spills:_x000D_ If a large amount of mercury is released, contact a professional cleaning service specializing in hazardous materials.

wasteCodes.practice: • Containers should not be washed and recycled/reused to be used as a container/pail • Disposed through a DENR-accredited TSD facility

Health-care waste should be disposed through a DENR-accredited TSD facility. • Sharps should all be collected together, regardless of whether or not they are contaminated. • Containers should be puncture-proof (usually made of metal or high-density plastic) and fitted with covers. They should be rigid and impermeable so that they safely retain not only the sharps but also any residual liquids from syringes. To discourage abuse, containers should be tamper-proof (difficult to open or break) and needles and syringes should be rendered unusable. Where plastic or metal containers are unavailable or too costly, containers made of dense cardboard are recommended (WHO, 1997); these fold for ease of transport and may be supplied with a plastic lining. • Bags and containers for infectious waste should be marked with the international infectious substance symbol • Highly infectious waste should, whenever possible, be sterilized immediately by autoclaving. It therefore needs to be packaged in bags that are compatible with the proposed treatment process: red bags, suitable for autoclaving, are recommended. • Cytotoxic waste, most of which is produced in major hospital or research facilities, should be collected in strong, leak-proof containers clearly labelled “Cytotoxic wastes”. • Small amounts of chemical or pharmaceutical waste may be collected together with infectious waste. • Large quantities of obsolete or expired pharmaceuticals stored in hospital wards or departments should be returned to the pharmacy for disposal. Other pharmaceutical waste generated at this level, such as spilled or contaminated drugs or packaging containing drug residues should not be returned because of the risk of contaminating the pharmacy; it should be deposited in the correct container at the point ofproduction. • Large quantities of chemical waste should be packed in chemical-resistant containers and sent to specialized treatment facilities. • The identity of the chemicals should be clearly marked on the containers: hazardous chemical wastes of different types should never be mixed. • Waste with a high content of heavy metals (e.g. cadmium or mercury) should be collected separately. • Aerosol containers may be collected with general health-care waste once they are completely empty, provided that the waste is not destined for incineration. • No healthcare waste other than sharps should be deposited in sharps containers, as these containers are more expensive than the bags used for other infectious waste. Measures of this sort help to minimize the costs of healthcare waste collection and treatment. When a disposable syringe is used, for example, the packaging should be placed in the general waste bin and the used syringe in the yellow sharps container. In most circumstances, the needle should not be removed from the syringe because of the risk of injury; if removal of the needle is required, special care must be taken. • Appropriate containers or bag holders should be placed in all locations where particular categories of waste may be generated. Instructions on waste separation and identification should be posted at each waste collection point to remind staff of the procedures. Containers should be removed when they are three- quarters full. • Staff should never attempt to correct errors of segregation by removing items from a bag or container after disposal or by placing one bag inside another bag of a different colour. • If general and hazardous wastes are accidentally mixed, the mixture should be treated as hazardous healthcare waste. Cultural and religious constraints in certain countries make it unacceptable for anatomical waste to be collected in the usual yellow bags; such waste should be disposed of in accordance with local custom, which commonly specifies burial.

Prevent product from entering sewer or confined spaces, waterways, soil or public waters. Do not flush to sewer. For spills on water, contain, minimize dispersion and collect. When cleaning non-disposable equipment, wear nitrile or other appropriate gloves (double gloving is recommended), goggles, and lab coat or other protective clothing. Prevent dispersion of particulates by wetting or dampening surfaces prior to clean up of equipment. If applicable, wash equipment using a bleach and detergent solution and then rinse with clean water.

wasteCodes.practice: Lead-acid batteries are used to start up the diesel generators (gensets) in the power plant. These batteries, which are made up of lead/lead oxide and sulfuric acid, are considered corrosive, toxic, and deleterious to both human health and the environment. Thus, lead – acid batteries should be handled and stored properly. The used lead-acid batteries at Bilangbilangan DPP shall be stored at the proposed HWSA. The batteries shall be stacked upright not more than four batteries high as to prevent the organic acids from leaking through the top vent holes. Spent lead-acid batteries are currently being stored inside the BDPP’s powerhouse. These will be transferred upon completion of the HWSA.

The Bilangbilangan DPP does not use mercury or any mercury-containing compounds in its operation per se. Instead, the other mercury-containing wastes generated come from discarded lighting fixtures such as busted fluorescent lamps. The busted fluorescent lamps shall be placed/stored in drums/container. These containers shall be covered and placed in a secure and dry storage area. Currently, busted fluorescent lamps are kept inside the powerhouse and shall be transferred to the proposed HWSA upon its completion._x000D_ For busted fluorescent lamps, these shall not be sent to landfills instead to recycling centers that break lamps under special conditions and safely remove and recover mercury.

During genset maintenance, lubricating oil shall be drained from the engines into a container and replaced with new supply. The drained oil shall be transferred manually into drums/containers, which shall be stored at the proposed HWSA inside the Bilangbilangan DPP’s compound. Currently, used/waste oil are stored inside plastic drums inside BDPP’s powerhouse. These plastic drums shall be kept in the proposed HWSA upon completion._x000D_ The recovered oil shall be removed/scooped manually and transferred into the waste oil drums/containers. Engine/equipment washings shall be collected in containers and placed in drums for storage. Used/waste oil drums containers shall be tightly closed to prevent spillage.

Used oil/fuel filters shall be placed/stored in drums/container. Oiled rags shall be stored in the same manner. The containers shall be covered to prevent leaching of oil during rain, and accumulation of rainwater which could corrode the container.

wasteCodes.practice: Lead acid batteries are used to start up diesel generators (GenSets) in the Substation. The used lead-acid batteries at Samboan SS shall be stored at the HWSA. The batteries shall be stacked upright not more than four batteries high as to prevent the organic acids from leaking through the top vent holes. Used lead-acid batteries shall be turned over to reclaimers for recycling or disposed of through a DENR accredited transporter/treater.

Samboan SS does not use mercury or any mercury-containing compouds in its operation per se. Instead, the other mercury-containing wastes generated come from discarded lighting fixtures such as busted fluorescent lamps. The PCO ensures that discarded busted lamps are segregated properly and are handled carefully to prevent breakages during storage. Discarded busted lamps are contained in drums and are properly labelled.

Used paints referrred are those excess paints from facility and equipment maintenance as necessary. Excess paints are stored in their respective containers and are kept tightly closed to prevent spillage. These are placed inside the HWSA with secondary containment provisions in cases of spillages.

During Transformer/GenSet maintenance, lubricating oil shall be drained from the transformer/engines into a container and replaced with new supply. The drained oil shall be transferred manually into drums/containers, which shall be stored at thje designated HWSA inside the Samboan SS compound. Drains from the secondary containment of transformer/engine is directed into the oil-water separator. The recovered oil shall be removed/scooped manually from the oil-water separator and transferred into the waste oil drums/containers. Used/waste oil drums containers shall be tightly close to prevent spillage.
The oil contaminated materials shall be stored at the designated Hazardous Waste Storage Area. The oil contaminated materials shall be transferred manually into drums/containers for safe keeping.

All hazardous wastes must be stored in appropriate leak-free containers according to their waste classification._x000D_ _x000D_ Type Content_x000D_ Polyethylene Drums/Containers Acids and Bases_x000D_ Metal Drums/Containers Flammable, Solvents, and Paints_x000D_ Fiber Drums/Containers Granular materials_x000D_ _x000D_ b. All hazardous wastes generated must be segregated to avoid reactions and/or mixing._x000D_ c. The storage facility must be enclosed but adequately ventilated._x000D_ d. The storage facility should only be accessed by authorized personnel._x000D_ e. Waste with chemical properties must be placed in separate containers and kept in a separate double containment areas._x000D_ f. Emergency equipment should be available at all times._x000D_ g. Training and appropriate PPEs should be provided for the personnel maintaining the area._x000D_ _x000D_ Transport and Disposal_x000D_ _x000D_ a. A 3rd party accredited transporter and treater by the DENR is the only contractor allowed to haul the hazardous wastes of the project._x000D_ b. All disposal of hazardous waste must be written in manifest form._x000D_ d. The proponent must follow the pre-transport requirements._x000D_ ● Container must be completely closed and sealed. If a container is damaged or corroded, wastes must be transferred to a new container._x000D_ ● Overloading of carts/containers is strictly prohibited._x000D_ _x000D_ Recording and Monitoring_x000D_ _x000D_ a. The establishment must record the generation, storage and disposal of hazardous waste thru Self-Monitoring Report and submit to DENR-EMB Region VI every quarter._x000D_ b. Certificate of Treatment (COT) should be issued to the proponent by the accredited treater of DENR after proper treatment of the hazardous wastes. In case of chemical spillage, the proponent shall notify the EMB within 24 hours by submitting an incident report to EMB.

wasteCodes.practice: Lead-acid batteries are used to start up the diesel generators (gensets) in the power plant. These batteries, which are made up of lead/lead oxide and sulfuric acid, are considered corrosive, toxic, and deleterious to both human health and the environment. Thus, lead – acid batteries should be handled and stored properly. The used lead-acid batteries at Camotes DPP shall be stored at the HWSA. The batteries shall be stacked upright not more than four batteries high as to prevent the organic acids from leaking through the top vent holes.

The Camotes DPP does not use mercury or any mercury-containing compounds in its operation per se. Instead, the other mercury-containing wastes generated come from discarded lighting fixtures such as busted fluorescent lamps. The busted fluorescent lamps shall be placed/stored in drums/container. These containers shall be covered and placed in a secure and dry storage area._x000D_ For busted fluorescent lamps, these shall not be sent to landfills instead to recycling centers that break lamps under special conditions and safely remove and recover mercury.

During genset maintenance, lubricating oil shall be drained from the engines into a container and replaced with new supply. The drained oil shall be transferred manually into drums/containers, which shall be stored at the designated HWSA inside the Camotes DPP’s compound. _x000D_ _x000D_ The recovered oil shall be removed/scooped manually and transferred into the waste oil drums/containers. Engine/equipment washings shall be collected in containers and placed in drums for storage. Used/waste oil drums containers shall be tightly closed to prevent spillage.

Used oil/fuel filters shall be placed/stored in drums/container. Oiled rags shall be stored in the same manner as the used oil. The containers shall be covered to prevent leaching of oil during rain, and accumulation of rainwater which could corrode the container.

wasteCodes.practice: COLLECTION:_x000D_ Collection shall refer to the act removing solid waste from the source or from a communal storage point_x000D_ _x000D_ WASTE HANDLING AND STORAGE:_x000D_ 1. Items classified as waste will be handled with care in accordance with legislative requirements _x000D_ 2. All waste will be stored in safe and secure manner pending collection in a storage container for _x000D_ disposal/recycling. _x000D_ 3. All waste will be stored in a manner that prevents its escape. _x000D_ 4. Wherever possible, access to waste containers will be restricted to the Company’s designated employees, contractors and contracted waste collection contractors. 5. Liquid wastes shall be stored in containers appropriate for the properties of the waste. Such containers will be stored with secondary containment or in a suitably bounded area. _x000D_ 6. Waste produce by contractors will be stored in designated areas and in dedicated sealed containers as provided by contractor, unless otherwise agreed by Factory Manager / Assistant EHSS Manager, Contractors will demonstrate 6S over any waste produced by them on the site. _x000D_ 7. At locations where provision is made for the segregation of waste for recycling or reuse the containers / area will be clearly and appropriately labeled identified. _x000D_ _x000D_ DISPOSAL:_x000D_ 1. Waste produces by the Company will only be transported off site by a registered waste transporter. A copy of the waste transporter’s valid registration certificate must be obtained. Historical records of waste transfer should be retained for three years. 2. Copies of valid waste management licenses for the final destination of all waste shall be maintained on sites and records retained for three years. 3.Controlled waste will be segregated at source into waste requiring disposal and those for which recycling has been arranged. An estimate of the weekly volume of waste for off-site disposal / recycling will be recorded. Records of estimates will be based on an examination using weighing scale of the quantity / volume of waste in waste storage containers prior their removal off-site. _x000D_ 4. Containers will be inspected for extraneous articles within at least 24 hours before collection, where possible and practical. Extraneous articles will only be removed where it has been identified it is safe. _x000D_ 5. All waste transferred off-site will be accompanied by a waste transfer note, completed and containing information and in accordance with the relevant regulatory requirements and codes of practice. Copies of waste transfer notes will be available at all times and retained for three years. _x000D_ 6. Redundant IT equipment’s will be sent for recycling to an approved contractor wherever practical.

Brooms and regular vacuum cleaners should not be used to clean up broken fluorescent bulbs because they will spread the mercury. With chemical-resistant gloves on, you may carefully pick up larger pieces of glass and debris and place them on a paper towel or newspaper. Then, pick up smaller pieces of glass and dust them with pieces of sticky tape, and place them on the paper. If the debris is on a hard surface, wipe it with damp paper towels and place the paper towels on the paper. Carefully fold everything into the paper and place it in a plastic bag. Seal the plastic bag(s), label them properly, and promptly dispose of the waste through an accredited transporter and treater.

wasteCodes.practice: Since we’re just a small company under peza, the quantity of this hazardous waste that we generate is very minimal which tend to be inconsiderable for some Haulers._x000D_ It is also a big loss to our part as a waste generator in terms of price over quantity in transporting/treating and disposal of this hazardous waste._x000D_ As of now, our waste management practice is to temporarily place our generated busted/waste LED bulbs and LED tube lights to our hazardous waste storage until we reach the reasonable quantity of this hazardous waste. By that time we’ll then contact a DENR accredited Treater/Transporter to schedule for hauling._x000D_ It also give us enough time to look for a DENR accredited treater/transporter for this kind of waste since our third party hauler (CCTFI) is not accepting it for now due to the unavailability of the treatment process._x000D_ We also secure proper handling and storing of this hazardous waste to our hazardous waste storage. Attached also are the signage indicator as a hazard classification and waste label sheet.

In our company, we placed those battery to a special waste bin located at CNC machine area. After that, the collected battery will be transferred to hazardous waste storage area and wait for disposal which will be takeover by our 3rd party DENR accredited treater/transporter._x000D_ When replacing the battery on the machine, only authorized personnel can performed the process and also can handle those waste batteries. To ensure the safety of each authorized personnel, they are oblige to wear the prescribe PPE like static gloves while performing the procedure. _x000D_ After replacement, the waste battery will be place to the special waste bin and transfer to the Hazardous waste storage area for hauling. When transfer to the Hazardous Waste Storage Area we secured that it is properly stored in a container, properly labeled, packed with the appropriate hazardous waste Class and its different hazardous waste characteristics.
As of now, We placed this hazardous waste to our MRF while we're still on process of contacting a PEZA & DENR ACCREDITED HAULERS.

These chemicals are toxic & ignitable and each of this plays different roles in the production as one of the main chemicals they had used._x000D_ These are properly pack, secured with appropriate labels and symbols as its indicator. It is also properly transported and treated with our third party treater/transporter of waste. _x000D_ Below are the different usage and process of our waste in our production process._x000D_ _x000D_ Methanol- is used to clean the processed metal or plastic product both inside and outside (outside means those products that are waiting for the next process) the CNC (Computer Numerical Control) machine. Also, there are some instances where the production used this as an adhesive remover. They soaked the output to the container containing methanol to remove exist oil and adhesive on it. But this chemical is not only intended for the outputs, they also used it to clean the machine table as preparation for the next process. As safety precaution, they used proper PPE (Personal Protective Equipment) when handling these chemicals to prevent their selves from contamination._x000D_ Basically, the production consumed around more or less 50 liters of methanol per quarter. The volume may vary depends on the quantity of Job orders they had received. _x000D_ As for the waste methanol, it will automatically combine to the mixture of coolant and water inside the machine and after 3-6 months it will be removed from the machine chamber for replacement. The collected waste of coolant and water mixture together with the methanol will be placed to a container which is properly labeled and stored in the COOLANT STORAGE. Same goes to those waste methanol's that they had used for soaking and for cleaning the products outside the machine, after using they poured the waste chemical to the container containing mixture of coolant with water and methanol._x000D_ RP7/WD-40 - it serves as a lubricant in the production especially when they are doing an operation which involves metal products. This aerosol spray chemical helps to enhance the appearance of the finish product while in production process. Same in methanol, they also used this while the output is still attached to the machine and basically the waste of this chemical is mixed to the coolant and water mixture with a bit of methanol. Same process goes, stored in the machine chamber for 3-6 months after that it will be transfer to a container and placed in the coolant storage._x000D_ Rapid Quick Remover- is more alike in Methanol in terms of handling, uses and disposal but not like methanol this chemical is seldom used because it is a bit strong than other chemicals. The production used it for cleaning the rust in different parts of the machine, Rapid Quick Remover serves as the best aid for removing rust to those affected areas inside the machine. They also used it to those parts of the machine which had massive oil moisture because of evaporation. Lastly, they also used it for cleaning the products thoroughly to prevent existing oils and adhesives on it. Same to the other non-halogenated organic solvents above, the waste rapid quick remover will be collected and pour to a container containing a mixture of coolant and water with a bit of methanol and rp7/wd-40 on it._x000D_ To assure the safety of all the staffs involves in using this different chemicals, the company provides PPE for each of them. During the whole process they used those appropriate PPEs intended for their line of work and also for the chemicals that they’re using.

Since each of these chemicals plays different part in the production, we also had different waste practices apply to its specific usage and characterization. As a overall summary to our waste management practice, I101 waste is properly pack under our coolant storage, properly labeled together with the symbol indicator. It is also properly transport and treated with our third party hauler which is the cebu common treatment facility Inc._x000D_ Below are the usage and handling of our waste in our production process._x000D_ RENOLIN SC 68 (AIR COMPRESSOR OIL) – This chemical serves as a lubricant that helps the motor to regulate properly, in that way we can also prevent the motor to overheat. _x000D_ The production staffs are the ones who are directly exposed to this chemical because they’re also intended to monitor the oil gauge of the air compressor. They used this chemical at least once (1) or twice (2) a week putting a 300ml of it to the oil chamber in the air compressor having an approximately 1.5 Liters total per month. This actions and volume may vary depends on the oil gauge of the compressor. _x000D_ Also to maintain the efficiency of the motor, they practice to change and drained the oil in the oil chamber of the compressor once (1) a month. By this we can prevent sludge formation and overheat of the motor. When draining, the amount of discarded used oil is no longer the same to the estimated total amount input because of evaporation; some is distributed to its parts. Resulting to approximately more or less 500ml discarded waste oil in a month. The volume may also vary depends on the input volume and situations that can affect the stability of the oil._x000D_ The discarded hazardous waste oil will be collected and placed to a container under coolant storage. The metal container also holds waste coolant (LACTUCA LT 2 AP) with a bit mixture of some waste non- halogenated organic solvents like methanol, RP7 lubricant and rapid quick remover. These chemicals are mixed in a metal container and stored in the coolant storage for hauling._x000D_ RENOLIN B 68 PLUS (MACHINE OIL) – This hazardous chemical is only intended for our machine consumption. Because of its characteristics and good oiliness that prevent metal to metal contact thereby reducing, wear friction and power consumption it serves as a very effective and useful chemical in the production. Although it doesn’t really involved in any production processes but it keeps the machine in a good state._x000D_ The production staffs are the ones who monitors the level of the machine oil, they’re also refills it once or twice a week. They put approximately 250 ml – 300 ml amount of RENOLIN B 68 PLUS (machine oil) having a total volume intake of approximately 1 – 1.5 liters a month. The volume may vary depends on the level of remaining oil in the oil container. _x000D_ In this hazardous chemical, WE DON’T GENERATE WASTE OIL. The oil itself will circulate to different parts of the machine which cause of decreasing amount in the oil container; evaporation is also one of its factors. The oil evaporates which brings moisture inside the machine resulting to sludge formation in different parts and tools in the machine. Those sludge formations in different parts and tools is removed using wipe cloth / rags, in that way these materials will fall under another Hazardous waste class which is I104 (Oil- Contaminated materials) Waste rags that contaminated with RENOLIN B 68 PLUS (machine oil)._x000D_ LACTUCA LT 2 AP (COOLANT) – The production used this hazardous chemicals when conducting machining process to the products that they’re making. In order to achieve the perfect mixture of lubricant, the production staff mixed this hazardous chemical with a volume more or less 2.8 liters to a 100 liters/ 5 gallons of Purified water. _x000D_ Mixing it first before poring inside the machine chamber made it more efficient which also affects the appearance of the processed output. To secure also the safety of all the staffs involved, it’s always our protocol to wear proper and appropriate PPE’s when handling different types of hazardous chemicals._x000D_ The mixture will last for at least 3-6 months inside the machine chamber before discarded and replacement. The discarded hazardous waste oil is transferred to a metal container with proper labels and symbols then placed to coolant storage. We also secure that all the containers are properly sealed to prevent any incident in the future like oil spillage. Lastly, we install secondary containment to our metal drums to easily accumulate the spillage if ever.

In our company, we don't conduct on-site decontamination to our I104 waste/Oil-contaminated materials. What we do to our 2 oil-contaminated waste materials are a likely the same, it only differs when we do filtration to our machine generated waste._x000D_ One of our oil-contaminated waste materials is rags/wipe cloth which is a very useful in our production. After using it, the production staff placed those waste contaminated rags to a special waste bin located inside the production. The special waste bin is properly labeled and it also contained appropriate hazardous symbols on it which indicates the possible hazard those waste rags brings._x000D_ When the special waste bin gets full, the production staff will collect those contaminated rags and put to trash bag for packing. The collected bags will be stored to MRF while waiting for the scheduled hauling._x000D_ Second oil-contaminated waste materials is machine generated waste. After the production process, all these generated hazardous waste will be collected and placed in a small strainer at the back of the machine for primary straining. The following day, those first strained waste will be transfer to bigger strainer for final straining outside the machine. Using these methods, we can prevent oil spillage when storing this waste to our MRF. After our final straining, we gathered all these machine generated waste and transfer to a trash bag for packing we also secure the durability of the bags that can contained a longer duration when storing inside MRF._x000D_ As safety precaution, we strictly implement to all staffs involve to wear proper PPE (Personal Protected Equipment) when handling these waste materials and chemicals to prevent themselves from contamination and to any health hazard those waste bring._x000D_ After doing all those procedures and precautionary measures of insuring the safety as well as the proper waste handling, we transfer those packed waste to the MRF that serves as storage. This time all we need to do is to contact our third party hauler which is the CCTFI (CEBU COMMON TREATMENT FACILITY INC.) for hauling and wait for the scheduled date.

wasteCodes.practice: Guidelines for Storing, Handling, and Transporting Busted Fluorescent Lamps(BFLs)._x000D_ _x000D_ *Storing_x000D_ a.)BFLs must be collected in a manner that breakage is prevented. These should be placed back in their replacement container for maximum protection, if applicable ._x000D_ b.)Broken BFLs shall be contained in closed containers(i.e., Polyethylene Drums)._x000D_ c.) All stacks and containers shall be labeled with the standard Hazardous Waste Label and the Toxic Sticker._x000D_ d.)Safety officers shall ensure that used/BFLs /bulbs are surrendered to the hazardous waste storage facility._x000D_ _x000D_ *Handling _x000D_ a.)Only authorized personnel shall be allowed to handle and transfer BFLs._x000D_ b.)Personnel in charge at the designated storage areas shall ensure that these are kept in drums labeled with the Hazardous Waste Label and the Toxic Sticker._x000D_ c.)The assigned personnel in the hazardous waste Storage facility should keep records of the number of BFLs collected._x000D_ d.)Broken lamps shall be handled with more caution. To protect handlers from exposure to hazards(mercury vapor and broken glass), they shall wear proper PPE(respirators and leather gloves) in case of lamps accidentally break._x000D_ _x000D_ *Transporting_x000D_ a.) Ensure that there is a valid Permit to Tranfort for the BFLs for hauling at the time of transport._x000D_ b.)Ensure that the drums containing BFLs are properly sealed and labeled._x000D_ c.)Only DENR-EMB recognized transporters shall be allowed to transport E-waste._x000D_ d.)Immediately inform and notify DENR-EMB and the local authority in case of accidents _x000D_ e.)Comply with the warning signs, marking, and other requirements of the DENR for the Transport of hazardous waste and materials.

Guidelines_x000D_ A.Guidlines for Storing, Handling, and Transporting Used Industrial Oil Including Sludge_x000D_ _x000D_ *Storing_x000D_ a.)Used industrial oil including sludge shall be contained in drums properly sealed to avoid spillage. This is a combustible substance and must be protected against the source of ignition (sparks, flares, flames) at all times._x000D_ b.)Drum shall be stacked on pallets and directly on the ground or soil._x000D_ c.)Containers shall be labeled using the standard Hazardous Waste Labeling._x000D_ d.)Flooring shall be concrete to prevent seepage of oil to the ground in case of spillage._x000D_ e.)Area to be installed shall be with containment gutter to isolate/separate spills from contaminating ordinary water sewage system or deep well._x000D_ f.)Stacking in open yards shall be avoided to protect containers from direct sunlight and other elements to prevent corrosion and leaks._x000D_ _x000D_ *Handling_x000D_ a.)Only authorized personnel shall be allowed to handle and transfer waste oils._x000D_ b.)Spillage of waste oils shall be controlled by using sand from Oil Spill kits provided in the storage area. Collected solids should be placed in a separate container to be disposed of as oil-contaminated hazardous waste as well._x000D_ c.)Personnel handling waste oils and oil contaminated materials shall always wear PPE( such as safety glasses, rubber gloves, and boots)._x000D_ _x000D_ *Transporting_x000D_ a.) Guidelines for Storing, Handling and Transporting Used-Oil Contaminated Materials_x000D_ _x000D_ *Storing _x000D_ a.)Used oil-contaminated materials shall be contained in drums properly sealed to avoid spillage. This is a combustible substance and must be protected against the source of ignition (sparks, flares, flames) at all times._x000D_ b.)Drum shall be stacked on pallets and directly on the ground or soil._x000D_ c.)Containers shall be labeled using the standard Hazardous Waste Labeling._x000D_ d.)Flooring shall be concrete to prevent seepage of oil to the ground in case of spillage._x000D_ e.)Area to be installed shall be with containment gutter to isolate/separate spills from contaminating ordinary water sewage system or deep well._x000D_ f.)Stacking in open yards shall be avoided to protect containers from direct sunlight and other elements to prevent corrosion and leaks._x000D_ _x000D_ *Handling_x000D_ a.)Only the authorized personnel shall be allowed to handle and transfer used oil-contaminated materials_x000D_ b.)Personnel handling waste oil and oil-contaminated materials shall always wear PPE (such as safety glasses , rubber gloves, and rubber boots)._x000D_ _x000D_ *Transporting_x000D_ a.)Ensure that there is a valid permit to transport the Used-Oil Contaminated materials for hauling at the time of transport._x000D_ b.)Ensure that the drums containing used industrial oil are properly sealed and labeled._x000D_ c.)Only DENR-EMB recognized transporters shall be allowed to transport used industrial oil including sludge._x000D_ d.)Immediately inform and notify DENR-EMB and the local authority in case of accidents ._x000D_ e.)Comply with the warning signs, marking, and other requirements of the DENR for the Transport of hazardous waste and materials.

wasteCodes.practice: LED LIGHT BULBS LEDs do not contain mercury, which can be found in CFL bulbs. However, like all-electric equipment, LEDs contain hazardous materials like arsenic, nickel, lead, and silver. Storage • Store the LED light bulbs in a box or case to prevent breakage before use. • Handle fluorescent lights carefully to prevent breakage. Disposal LED bulbs need to be treated and disposed of similarly to other electronics. • Light bulb must be wrapped and taped everything in place or put in a container before disposing of the bulb. They are fragile and can break in the trash. Broken glass can injure garbage collectors. • Since LED lights do not utilize any chemical reactions, there is no need to wear a protective suit or hazmat while cleaning a broken bulb. • Suppose the capacitor inside the LED explodes and the bulb shatters into pieces, one can smell the fumes of typical electronic devices. In this case, the utility personnel or the person cleaning needs to wear mask and use gloves for protection. • Use the broom to sweep the floor or surface with the bulb components and put in a closed container labeled as “broken light bulb”. • Place all broken pieces and the bulb into a sealable container. This is to ensure garbage collectors do not hurt themselves with sharp glass pieces. • Place the container into the hazardous waste bin.

LED ACID BATTERIES Storage • Store the battery after fully charging it • Store it at room temperature or lower • Remove the battery from the equipment • Charge it every 6 months, or as recommended by the manual • Avoid deep discharge • Choose proper float voltages to avoid sulfation and corrosion For single-use batteries: • Place the batteries in a bag or tape them: To avoid a fire hazard, tape each end of the battery with clear, non-conductive tape to prevent residual discharge. If you do not have tape, each battery can be placed in its own plastic bag instead. • Store the batteries in a non-conductive container: Place the wrapped batteries in a cardboard box or plastic container. Do not place them in a metal box because they could spark causing a fire. For rechargeable batteries: • Take the old batteries out of the electronics: Make sure to remove the rechargeable batteries from your old electronics. Electronics will need to be recycled separately. • Tape or bag the batteries: Just like with single-use batteries, we want to safely tape or bag them for recycling. Once the batteries are safe for transport, they can be dropped them off at the nearest special recycling facility or collected by PASSI. They can be dropped off within 6 months once they are bagged or taped.

USED INDUSTRIAL OIL INCLUDING SLUDGE How Nephro Specialist of Liloan Inc. handles used oil: Nephro Specialist of Liloan Inc. is a business that handles used oil from their equipment i.e., generator set. In order to run the generator, it needs to be filled with 300 litres of diesel fuel. The generator is used if the power goes out to keep its essential equipment running, particularly the dialysis machines, which are used for its main operations. As a business that handles used oil, it is important that we follow good business practices to ensure the safe handling of used oil, to maximize recycling, and to minimize disposal. Storage, cleaning up leaks and spills: • Label all containers containing used oil as “USED OIL”. • Keep containers and tanks in good condition. Do not allow metal containers to rust leak or deteriorate. Fix structural defects immediately. • Never store used oil in anything other than storage containers. Used oil is stored in the hazardous waste bin at our material recycling facility (MRF). Oil leaks and spills: • Take steps to prevent leaks and spills. Keep machinery, equipment containers, and tanks in good working condition and be careful when transferring used oil. Have sorbent materials available on site. • If a spill or leak occurs, stop the oil from flowing at the source. If a leak from a container or tank can't be stopped, put the oil in another holding container. • Contain spilled oil. Containment can be accomplished by erecting sorbent berms or by spreading a sorbent over the oil and • Clean up the oil and recycle the used oil as you would have before it was spilled. If recycling is not possible, you first must make sure the used oil is not a hazardous waste and dispose of it appropriately. All used cleanup materials, from rags to sorbent booms, that contain free-flowing used oil also must be handled according to the used oil management standards. Remember, all leaked and spilled oil collected during cleanup must be handled as used oil. If you are a used oil handler, you should become familiar with these cleanup methods. They may also be part of a spill response action plan. • Remove, repair, or replace the defective container immediately. Cleanup practices: • Remove as much of the free-flowing oil as possible and manage the oil as you would have before it spilled if we have used oil on rags or other sorbent materials from cleaning up leak or spill. Conserving oil: • Minimise the amount of used oil you produce. The less used oil that is produced in the first place, the less that ultimately has to be handled. We can filter, separate and recondition used oil to prolong its usable life. • Practice safe management of used oil. Don’t mix used oil with anything. Always store used oil in leak-proof containers that are in secure areas safely away from workers and the environment. Send used oil to a re-refiner whenever possible.

OIL-CONTAMINATED MATERIALS Employee Roles and Responsibilities: • Ensure that oily rags and absorbents are being handled properly according to all applicable Department of Environmental and Natural Resources (DENR) and Environmental Management Bureau (EMB) laws, policies and guidelines • Ensure employees are properly trained to manage absorbent waste. • Confer with their Pollution Control Officer (PCO) if they have any questions about how to manage their absorbent waste. • Minimize the volumes of waste absorbents that are generated during processes. Disposal Rags, absorbent cloths and other absorbents used to clean up oil spills should be placed in the trash. To avoid spontaneous combustion, place oil-contaminated materials in a metal container with a tight fitting lid. Rags, towels and absorbents contaminated with oil and grease are not considered hazardous waste, unless they are contaminated with any of EMB’s list of hazardous solvents. If small quantities of oily shop towels or absorbents are generated, then these can be discarded in the general trash. However, if waste oily rags and absorbents are generated on a regular basis, then a waste must be put in the hazardous waste container in the MRF. The container should be lined with a compatible liner (such as a clear plastic bag), properly labeled as oily rags, and closed when not in use. Even though absorbents contaminated with oil are not classified as hazardous waste, they still need to be managed properly, according to DENR’s used oil. Pollution Abatement Systems Specialists Inc. (PASSI) can be contacted to help set up a collection container and advise on properly managing and disposing this waste. If an oil spill is large (more than one gallon), or enters a storm drain, PASSI must be immediately contacted including the fire department, and evacuate the area. The spill should be contained as soon as possible. Spill kits are stored for use in the event of a spill.
We have a Material Recovery Facility for the separation of waste and have the PASSI or pollution abatement systems specialists inc. to pick up the infectious waster every after 2 weeks.

wasteCodes.practice: LED LIGHT BULBS_x000D_ LEDs do not contain mercury, which can be found in CFL bulbs. However, like all-electric equipment, LEDs contain hazardous materials like arsenic, nickel, lead, and silver._x000D_ Storage_x000D_ • Store the LED light bulbs in a box or case to prevent breakage before use. _x000D_ • Handle fluorescent lights carefully to prevent breakage._x000D_ _x000D_ Disposal_x000D_ LED bulbs need to be treated and disposed of similarly to other electronics._x000D_ • Light bulb must be wrapped and taped everything in place or put in a container before disposing of the bulb. They are fragile and can break in the trash. Broken glass can injure garbage collectors. _x000D_ • Since LED lights do not utilize any chemical reactions, there is no need to wear a protective suit or hazmat while cleaning a broken bulb._x000D_ • Suppose the capacitor inside the LED explodes and the bulb shatters into pieces, one can smell the fumes of typical electronic devices. In this case, the utility personnel or the person cleaning needs to wear mask and use gloves for protection._x000D_ • Use the broom to sweep the floor or surface with the bulb components and put in a closed container labeled as “broken light bulb”. _x000D_ • Place all broken pieces and the bulb into a sealable container. This is to ensure garbage collectors do not hurt themselves with sharp glass pieces._x000D_ • Place the container into the hazardous waste bin.

LED ACID BATTERIES_x000D_ _x000D_ Storage_x000D_ • Store the battery after fully charging it_x000D_ • Store it at room temperature or lower_x000D_ • Remove the battery from the equipment_x000D_ • Charge it every 6 months, or as recommended by the manual_x000D_ • Avoid deep discharge_x000D_ • Choose proper float voltages to avoid sulfation and corrosion_x000D_ For single-use batteries: _x000D_ • Place the batteries in a bag or tape them: To avoid a fire hazard, tape each end of the battery with clear, non-conductive tape to prevent residual discharge. If you do not have tape, each battery can be placed in its own plastic bag instead. _x000D_ • Store the batteries in a non-conductive container: Place the wrapped batteries in a cardboard box or plastic container. Do not place them in a metal box because they could spark causing a fire._x000D_ For rechargeable batteries:_x000D_ • Take the old batteries out of the electronics: Make sure to remove the rechargeable batteries from your old electronics. Electronics will need to be recycled separately._x000D_ • Tape or bag the batteries: Just like with single-use batteries, we want to safely tape or bag them for recycling. _x000D_ Once the batteries are safe for transport, they can be dropped them off at the nearest special recycling facility or collected by PASSI. They can be dropped off within 6 months once they are bagged or taped.

USED INDUSTRIAL OIL INCLUDING SLUDGE_x000D_ How Nephro Specialist of Liloan Inc. handles used oil:_x000D_ Nephro Specialist of Liloan Inc. is a business that handles used oil from their equipment i.e., generator set. In order to run the generator, it needs to be filled with 300 litres of diesel fuel. The generator is used if the power goes out to keep its essential equipment running, particularly the dialysis machines, which are used for its main operations._x000D_ As a business that handles used oil, it is important that we follow good business practices to ensure the safe handling of used oil, to maximize recycling, and to minimize disposal. _x000D_ Storage, cleaning up leaks and spills:_x000D_ • Label all containers containing used oil as “USED OIL”._x000D_ • Keep containers and tanks in good condition. Do not allow metal containers to rust leak or deteriorate. Fix structural defects immediately._x000D_ • Never store used oil in anything other than storage containers. Used oil is stored in the hazardous waste bin at our material recycling facility (MRF)._x000D_ Oil leaks and spills:_x000D_ • Take steps to prevent leaks and spills. Keep machinery, equipment containers, and tanks in good working condition and be careful when transferring used oil. Have sorbent materials available on site._x000D_ • If a spill or leak occurs, stop the oil from flowing at the source. If a leak from a container or tank can't be stopped, put the oil in another holding container._x000D_ • Contain spilled oil. Containment can be accomplished by erecting sorbent berms or by spreading a sorbent over the oil and_x000D_ • Clean up the oil and recycle the used oil as you would have before it was spilled. If recycling is not possible, you first must make sure the used oil is not a hazardous waste and dispose of it appropriately. All used cleanup materials, from rags to sorbent booms, that contain free-flowing used oil also must be handled according to the used oil management standards. Remember, all leaked and spilled oil collected during cleanup must be handled as used oil. If you are a used oil handler, you should become familiar with these cleanup methods. They may also be part of a spill response action plan._x000D_ • Remove, repair, or replace the defective container immediately._x000D_ _x000D_ Cleanup practices:_x000D_ • Remove as much of the free-flowing oil as possible and manage the oil as you would have before it spilled if we have used oil on rags or other sorbent materials from cleaning up leak or spill. _x000D_ Conserving oil:_x000D_ • Minimise the amount of used oil you produce. The less used oil that is produced in the first place, the less that ultimately has to be handled. We can filter, separate and recondition used oil to prolong its usable life._x000D_ • Practice safe management of used oil. Don’t mix used oil with anything. Always store used oil in leak-proof containers that are in secure areas safely away from workers and the environment. Send used oil to a re-refiner whenever possible.

OIL-CONTAMINATED MATERIALS_x000D_ Employee Roles and Responsibilities:_x000D_ • Ensure that oily rags and absorbents are being handled properly according to all applicable Department of Environmental and Natural Resources (DENR) and Environmental Management Bureau (EMB) laws, policies and guidelines_x000D_ • Ensure employees are properly trained to manage absorbent waste._x000D_ • Confer with their Pollution Control Officer (PCO) if they have any questions about how to manage their absorbent waste._x000D_ • Minimize the volumes of waste absorbents that are generated during processes._x000D_ Disposal_x000D_ Rags, absorbent cloths and other absorbents used to clean up oil spills should be placed in the trash. To avoid spontaneous combustion, place oil-contaminated materials in a metal container with a tight fitting lid._x000D_ Rags, towels and absorbents contaminated with oil and grease are not considered hazardous waste, unless they are contaminated with any of EMB’s list of hazardous solvents. If small quantities of oily shop towels or absorbents are generated, then these can be discarded in the general trash. However, if waste oily rags and absorbents are generated on a regular basis, then a waste must be put in the hazardous waste container in the MRF. The container should be lined with a compatible liner (such as a clear plastic bag), properly labeled as oily rags, and closed when not in use. Even though absorbents contaminated with oil are not classified as hazardous waste, they still need to be managed properly, according to DENR’s used oil. Pollution Abatement Systems Specialists Inc. (PASSI) can be contacted to help set up a collection container and advise on properly managing and disposing this waste. If an oil spill is large (more than one gallon), or enters a storm drain, PASSI must be immediately contacted including the fire department, and evacuate the area. The spill should be contained as soon as possible. Spill kits are stored for use in the event of a spill.
All the infectious waste will be separated to MRF waste and to be collected with the Pollution abatement system specialist Inc.

wasteCodes.practice: Busted flourescent and LED lamps are packed separately. Busted long LED lamps are placed in used boxes and tape the ends to secure the box. Boxes are kept in a secure, dry place. The packed boxes are single piled and some are placed vertically in plastic drums. LED bulbs are placed drums with cover. Boxes and drums are labeled 'HAZARDOUS WASTE' in a laminated yellow paper (8.5x11') including its hazardous property, waste description, waste class and number, generator's name, address and contact person, and date of accumulation. TOXIC symbol in laminated placard (25 x 25 cm)) is also posted along with the yellow label. All packed LED busted lamps are placed in 'BUSTED LAMPS STORAGE AREA'. Inventory of new busted lamp are done twice a week and added to the existing ones. Disposal of the busted LED will be done after completing the requirements and approval of the Hazardous Waste Generator ID registration. Disposal will be done by an DENR accredited hauler and treater.
The current practice is returning back the used lead acids batteries to the supplier when bought a new one.

Long busted are placed in used boxes and tape the ends to secure the box. Boxes are kept in a secure, dry place. The packed boxes are single piled and some are placed vertically in plastic drums. Bulbs are placed drums with cover. Boxes and drums are labeled 'HAZARDOUS WASTE' in a laminated yellow paper (8.5x11') including its hazardous property, waste description, waste class and number, generator's name, address and contact person, and date of accumulation. TOXIC symbol in laminated placard (25 x 25 cm)) is also posted along with the yellow label. All packed busted lamps are placed in 'BUSTED LAMPS STORAGE AREA'. Inventory of new busted lamp are done twice a week and added to the existing ones. Disposal of the busted will be done after completing the requirements and approval of the Hazardous Waste Generator ID registration. Disposal will be done by an DENR accredited hauler and treater.

There is no collected oil and grease from kitchen grease traps in the campus. Food concessionaires are not allowed to cook inside the campus. Scraping of sauce and gravy from the used plate are also done before washing them to avoid accumulating grease in the grease trap and clogging of drain pipes. In case there will be a grease collected from the grease traps, the solidified oil and grease will be strained and placed inside a wide mouth HDPE container with lid. The container will be labelled as HAZARDOUS WASTE-FLAMMABLE SOLID. The filled container will be temporarily stored at 'USED OIL STORAGE AREA'. Hauling and treatment of grease will be done by a DENR accredited hauler and treater.

Used oil from generator set is placed in a 20-Li plastic (HDPE) container with lid. All containers are labeled 'HAZARDOUS WASTE' printed in a laminated yellow paper (8.5x11') with hazardous waste information such as hazardous property, waste description, waste class and number, generator's name and contact person, and date of accumulation. FLAMMABLE symbol in laminated placard is also posted along with the yellow label. All filled containers are placed in a plastic second containment to avoid spilling into the waterways or ground in case of container damage/breakage. They are stored in a well ventilated storage area. Sawdust are on standby and used to absorb oil spill in case of oil leaking to the ground. Fire extinguisher is also installed near the area. Recording of new waste oil is done right after the endorsing it to the PCO office for proper labeling. Disposal of used oil will be done upon completion and approval of the Hazardous Waste Generator ID registration and it will be done by DENR accredited hauler and treater.

Used oil from kitchen laboratory is placed in a 20-Li plastic (HDPE) container with lid. All containers are labeled 'HAZARDOUS WASTE' printed in a laminated yellow paper (8.5x11') with hazardous waste information such as hazardous property, waste description, waste class and number, generator's name and contact person, and date of accumulation. FLAMMABLE symbol in laminated placard is also posted along with the yellow label. All filled containers are placed in a plastic second containment to avoid spilling into the waterways or ground in case of container damage/breakage. They are stored in a well ventilated storage area. Sawdust are on standby and used to absorb oil spill in case of oil leaking to the ground. Fire extinguisher is also installed near the area. Recording of new waste oil is done right after the endorsing it to the PCO office for proper labeling. Disposal of used oil will be done upon completion and approval of the Hazardous Waste Generator ID registration and it will be done by DENR accredited hauler and treater.

As of this time, no oil-contaminated materials are collected. If these materials are collected/generated, this will be placed in a separate container with lid and will be labelled as HAZARDOUS WASTE - FLAMMABLE SOLID. The container will also be placed inside the OIL STORAGE AREA.

In some cases, damaged laboratory electronic equipment will be traded back into the supplier to get discounts. Old model CPU's and monitors are donated to some public schools but for the unrepairable electronic equipment are sold to scrap buyer at extremely low price. The scrap buyer will be the one who will sell to the recycling company who are accredited by DENR. The plan of the University will be disposing the damaged electronic equipment directly to the DENR accredited recyclers. Hauling and treating/recycling those equipment will be processed according the DENR HW guidelines.
As of this time, damaged white goods are sold to junk buyer for repair, reusing, repurposing and recycling.

Drains from the secondary containment of transformer/ engine is directed into the oil-water separator. The recovered oil shall be removed/scooped manually from the Oil-Water separator and transferred into the waste oil drums/containers. Used/waste oil drums containers shall be tightly close to prevent spoillage.

wasteCodes.practice: (1) Transportation, Labelling and Storage of Hazardous waste at the Hazardous waste storage house. The hazardous waste in the container/drum shall be transported to the hazardous waste storage house with the corresponding Hazardous Waste Label and appropriate GHS hazard and transport pictograms. The quantity/volume of waste must be recorded for monitoring. It must be inspected to ensure that the drum/container containing the waste doesn’t have leaks before storing the waste. The hazardous waste in the hazardous waste storage house must be ensure that that liquid or sludge wastes are placed in a secondary containment to prevent spills/leaks and from entering into the drainage or sewerage system. (2) Pull-out/collection of Hazardous Waste by an Accredited Transporter. The hazardous waste must be pull-out by an accredited transporter and TSD facility. Upon hazardous waste pull-out, it must be ensure that the Transporter have the following: Valid Transport Permit, Hazardous Waste Manifest Form, and must refer to the Transport Permit on the quantity or volume permitted/granted by DENR. The manifest form must be properly fill-up and shall be prepared every transport. The accredited hazardous waste transporter shall pull-out/collect the hazardous waste stored at the hazardous waste storage house and transport the waste to the TSD Facility. The accredited TSD Facility shall properly treat, store and dispose the hazardous wastes off-site. We shall coordinate with the TSD Facility and shall obtain CERTIFICATE OF TREATMENT (COT) for the waste treated to be filed for record keeping and reference.
